findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the three destination cards (Canggu, Uluwatu, Kuta Lombok), at desktop and phone
findings.fault: The cards look like links, but nothing happens when you click them. Each is a raised white card with a 'Best hostels' label and a chevron, and it has a hover rule. The parts map says all three are static. The page's second job is to send visitors to the destination guides, and this is the only place it offers them. A visitor who taps 'Canggu' gets nothing and has no other way to reach a guide.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who wants to know where to stay in Canggu or Kuta Lombok. They tap the card and nothing happens, so they decide the site is broken or empty and leave.

findings.where: Nav 'How we rank', and the footer's 'How we rank', 'Privacy', 'Terms' and 'Report content'
findings.fault: All five links point back to this same page. The hero's one selling point is ranking 'on merit alone', and the link that should explain it goes nowhere. The privacy and terms links are dead too.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who has been burned by paid placements on booking sites. They click 'How we rank' to check the merit claim and land back where they started. To them the claim now looks like marketing with nothing behind it.

findings.where: Hero: the coral primary CTA 'Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news'
findings.fault: The launch-news sign-up is a mailto link. It opens a blank email to someone called Luc, with no subject and no hint of what to write. Nothing says what they'll get, how often, or that they can stop it. Many phone and webmail users have no mail app set up, so the tap may open nothing or an unfamiliar app. The long label also wraps to two lines in the pill at phone width.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who would leave an address for launch news. Writing a cold email to a stranger, unsure what to say or what will follow, is far more effort than typing an address, so most won't do it.

findings.where: Hero headline block at desktop and phone: the eyebrow 'The better way to find hostels in Indonesia.', the h1 'MantaHostels', and the paragraph under it
findings.fault: The biggest type in the hero is the brand name, which the nav bar already shows directly above. The actual claim sits in a small eyebrow above it. The one sentence that says what this is (a merit-ranked search that isn't live yet and sends you to book with the hostel) is the smallest text in the hero.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning for five seconds. They read the logo twice and 'the better way', a vague claim, and miss that the search isn't open yet and how it differs from the booking sites.

findings.fault: The section heading, two lines of display type at about 120 px, is far bigger than the hero's h1. In the whole-page view it is what you notice first, ahead of the hero and its CTA. A plain label for three cards outranks the page's claim and action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the page. A label for three cards is louder than the page's actual message, so the order of importance reads backwards and the three small cards look like an afterthought under it.

findings.where: Footer tagline 'Launching across Indonesia · piloting now in Bali' against the Kuta Lombok card
findings.fault: The footer says the pilot is in Bali, but the section above lists Kuta Lombok as one of the places 'where we're starting'. The page contradicts itself on where the product is.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker planning a Bali-and-Lombok trip. They can't tell whether Lombok is covered yet, and two conflicting statements make the rest of the copy less believable.

findings.where: Destination cards: the borders and shadows, desktop and phone
findings.fault: Each card has a thick purple border, a colour found nowhere else on the page or in the brand, and a heavy, wide shadow while at rest. Beside the turquoise, sand and ink, the purple looks like a stray default or a different site.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor judging whether this is a finished, trustworthy product. The off-palette purple and heavy shadows look unfinished and break the beachy look the hero sets up.

findings.where: Destination cards: the place eyebrows (BALI, LOMBOK) and the city names, desktop and phone
findings.fault: The city names and region eyebrows are set in a typewriter-style monospace font. Every other heading on the page uses the rounded brand display face. They read like code or placeholder text, not destination names.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading the cards. The switch to a code-like font makes the destinations look like an unstyled draft, not inviting places to stay.

findings.where: Nav bar, desktop: 'Destinations' and 'How we rank'
findings.fault: The two nav links are styled differently. 'How we rank' is underlined and 'Destinations' is bold with no underline. Bold without an underline is how the site marks the current page, so 'Destinations' reads as the page you're already on.
findings.who_objects: A visitor finding their way around. They may think they're already in a Destinations section and skip that link.

findings.where: Hero buttons: the coral pill CTA and the 'Explore destinations' outline button
findings.fault: The two buttons, stacked one above the other, have unrelated shapes: a fully rounded pill and a sharp-cornered rectangle with a thin ink outline on the turquoise. The pair looks as if it came from two different kits.
findings.who_objects: A visitor forming a first impression. The mismatched controls make the hero look less finished.

findings.where: Hero on desktop: the text column and the mascot on the ink wave band
findings.fault: The hero text starts about 230 px further right than the nav logo, the section heading and the cards, which all share one left edge. The right half of the hero is empty. The mascot sits alone at the far right edge in a mostly empty ink band, away from everything else.
findings.who_objects: A visitor scanning the page. The shifted column and the stranded mascot make the layout look unplanned, not like one deliberate composition.
